_note: Session 30: the abandoned mineshaft's texts (encounters/Mineshaft.js; DESIGN.md "Abandoned mineshaft"). Every text is a draft for Aaron. The story they tell (my draft, Session 30): the Black Laurel Coal Company's No. 2 shaft shut in 1987 after bad air in the low seam. A few weeks ago the army opened it again: something on their instruments, far down. They hired back the old foreman and a crew of men who'd worked it, to run the hoist and timber the low seam for them. Eleven went down on the last shift and never tagged out. What the army brought up before that, they brought up in a net, sedated (the outpost's container).
sign: BLACK LAUREL COAL CO. No. 2 SHAFT. CLOSED 1987. And under it, stencilled, a lot newer: U.S. GOVT PROPERTY. NO ENTRY.

searches.text: A requisition, three weeks old: timber, cable, eleven men's wages, signed for by an army captain. Under it the foreman's own hand: "They don't want coal. They want the low seam opened. Nobody will say why."
A brass tag on a hook for every man below. You hang it going down, you take it coming up. Eleven still hang there.
Cap lamps on a dead charger, flat, every one. One's missing off the end. You strip the rest for what's in them.
A thermos, a photo of a girl on a pony, a box of pistol rounds, a first aid tin. And his tag. He hadn't gone down. He isn't here either.
Rifle rounds. A crate stencilled TRANQUILLISER, LARGE ANIMAL, empty. A cargo net big enough for a horse, cut clean through from the inside.
Coal, spilled. In it a thread as thick as your thumb, pale, and tacky when you touch it. It runs back toward the shaft.

box.prompt: fit a battery to the lift
box.none: The lift's control box. The battery tray's empty and the leads are hanging. A car battery would do it.
box.done: The leads bite. A relay clacks in the hoist house, and a lamp comes on in the cage.

cage.dead: The cage. The lever does nothing: no power
cage.hang: The cage stops dead. Somewhere a long way up, the drum groans. Then it lets go.
cage.landed: Bottom of the shaft. It's warm down here, and the air's thick. A cart with a gun bolted to it sits on the rails, pointing down the drift.

winch.prompt: hook the cart to the haulage rope and go back up

cart.winched: The haulage rope takes the cart back up the drift, slow, the whole way in the dark.

points.halt: The cart grinds to a stop. The points are set for the siding, and the siding's under the roof. There's a lever on a stand up ahead on the right.
points.done: The lever goes over and the blades clack across. The way's open.

fall.prompt: lever the rock off the rails
fall.halt: Rock down across the rails. There's a pinch bar beside it.
fall.done: The last of it rolls clear. The rails are bent, not broken. It'll run.

bottom.arrive: The cart fetches up against the buffers. End of the drift. Ahead, a timber bulkhead right across it, barred from this side, and strung all over with something pale. There's a light under it, red, and it's humming.

door.prompt: lever the bar out with the pinch bar
door.done: The bar shrieks out of its brackets and the leaf sags. You drag it back against the wall. The air that comes through is warm, and it smells of singed hair.

bottom.inside: This was never dug. A cavern, the roof lost in the dark. At the far end the coal's split from the floor up, and the split is lit from inside, red, coming and going like breath. Beside it something the size of a car hangs from the roof, torn open.
bottom.roost: The roof's moving. They're all up there in the silk, folded, and every eye is on the seam. Not one of them looks at you.
bottom.hint: Nobody's coming back down here after you. Anything worth carrying out, take it now.

seam.text: A hand wide. It isn't fire: there's no heat off it, and the hum's in your teeth. There's no back to it either. A long way of red, and far off in it something moving, the way things move under ice.

cocoon.prompt: look at the thing hung from the roof
cocoon.text: Silk, wound as thick as a mattress, twice your height. It split down one side from the inside, and the edges have curled and gone hard. Empty. What came out of it was taller than you, and it came out folded.

foreman.prompt: look at the man by the box
foreman.text: Sixty, about. FOREMAN on his hard hat. There isn't a bite on him. He ran the cable back from the face, sat down to get his breath, and didn't get it. His hand's a foot short of the plunger.

log.prompt: take the book by his hand

sticks.prompt: take the sticks left in the open case
sticks.text: Dynamite, dry, the paper still stiff. The rest of the case went into the wall.
sticks.full: You can't carry any more dynamite. The sticks stay in the case.

drill.prompt: knock the head off the rock drill
drill.keep: The rock drill's head: a ram for the front of the dozer, one day

plunger.armed: The handle goes down like it's going through gravel. Nothing. Then a spit and a fizz by your boot: they spliced in a length of slow fuse, to give the shot-firer time to reach the cart. It's burning. Go.
plunger.late: You're still on your feet in the drift when it goes.

board.prompt: jump in and throw the rope's clutch

out.haul: The haulage rope snatches the cart and starts it back up the drift at a walk. Ahead of you the moths are pouring away up it, every one of them, and not one looks back.
out.blast: It goes. You feel it in the rails before you hear it. Then the whole drift behind you is orange, and the cart is going a great deal faster than the rope.
out.rails: There are men on the rails ahead. Every one you hit slows you down.
out.singe: The fire comes right over the cart's tail and you with it, and falls back. Keep the rails clear.
out.sealed: The ground thumps once under your boots. Smoke comes up the shaft like a chimney's, and the cage hangs crooked in the collar. Whatever's down there is under a mountain now.
out.lever: The cage hangs crooked in the collar and the shaft's breathing smoke. Nothing's going down there again
out.box: The lift's control box. The relay's tripped for good

fight.first: There's a man on the rails ahead, in a hard hat, his back to you. He turns round. He's been dead a while.
fight.roost: Red points of light up under the roof timbers ahead. Dozens of them. Eyes.
fight.woke: They drop off the timbers all at once and come down the drift after the cart.
fight.scattered: The roost bursts apart. Most of them go, away down the drift. Not all.
fight.beetles: Something big comes up out of the ballast ahead.
fight.steep: The drift tips over and the cart runs away with you. The brake's doing nothing.
fight.left: They break off, every one of them at once, and go over the top of the bulkhead like smoke up a flue.
